native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: Original papers in Experimental Economics (project=='ee') average 28.00 pages (median 27.5, sd 7.37, n=18 unique originals, 2011-2014). Original papers in Psychology (project=='rpp') average 11.01 pages (median 9.0, sd 6.21, n=88 unique originals, 2008-2015). Within Psychology, Social originals (n=46) average 11.70 pages and Cognitive originals (n=42) average 10.26 pages; both sub-disciplines remain below the Experimental Economics mean. The gap is robust to two sensitivities: including drop==True rows raises the rpp mean to 11.23 (n=95), and row-level (no de-duplication of repeat replication pairs) gives 11.00 (n rows=90); ee is unchanged across scenarios because no ee row carries the drop flag and no ee original is repeated.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (927 rows x 57 cols). Confirmed length is integer pages of original and project encodes the four replication projects. Filtered to project in {ee, rpp}; default excludes drop==True. Collapsed on title+authors.o+journal+pub_year to obtain unique original papers (88 in rpp; 18 in ee). Computed mean/median/std/min/max/IQR for ee and rpp, plus a parallel discipline split for Psychology (Social vs Cognitive). Reported two sensitivities: include drop==True rows, and row-level without de-duplication. Wrote analysis.py, analysis.ipynb (nbformat v4 with executed stream outputs), results.json and length_summary.csv.

Within Psychology, Social originals (n=46) average 11.70 pages and Cognitive originals (n=42) average 10.26 pages; both sub-disciplines remain below the Experimental Economics mean.
